gaps.sentence: You will not pass the course unless you ___ all the assignments.
gaps.hint: unless means if not, present simple
gaps.explanation: 'Unless' introduces a negative condition and takes the present simple: complete.

gaps.sentence: I will tell her the news when I ___ her at the party.
gaps.hint: when clauses take present for future
gaps.explanation: Time clauses with future meaning use the present simple, not 'will': see.

gaps.sentence: I'll lend you the tent ___ you bring it back dried.
gaps.explanation: 'Provided (that)' introduces the condition under which something will happen.

gaps.sentence: If you ___ a muscle, apply ice at once.
gaps.hint: medical instruction, present simple after if
gaps.explanation: The if-clause of a conditional instruction uses the present simple, never 'will': pull.

gaps.sentence: But ___ the late equaliser, United would have gone top of the table.
gaps.hint: but ___ = if it had not been for
gaps.explanation: 'But for + noun' is an implied conditional: had it not been for the equaliser…

gaps.sentence: I wish I ___ taller, but genes are genes.
gaps.hint: an impossible present wish with were
gaps.explanation: For impossible present wishes, formal English uses 'were': were.

gaps.sentence: If the route ___ safer, I would cycle to work.
gaps.hint: an imaginary present situation, subjunctive were
gaps.explanation: Unreal present conditions formally take 'were' rather than 'is': were.

gaps.sentence: He wishes he ___ harder at school when he had the chance.
gaps.hint: past regret, wish plus past perfect
gaps.explanation: Regret about past behavior takes the past perfect after 'wish': had worked.
